title: Implement a Dead-Letter Queue for Transformation Failures
description: The SpotLight Streams ETL Forge processes critical data streams. Currently, when a message fails during the transformation stage (e.g., due to malformed data or a processing bug), the `transform-worker` service logs the error and discards the message. This leads to silent data loss. The goal is to introduce a more robust error-handling mechanism by implementing a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ). Failed messages must be rerouted to a dedicated Kafka topic for later analysis and reprocessing. This task will be performed over multiple sessions, starting with investigation, followed by implementation, and finally refinement and documentation.

project_spec.name: SpotLight Streams ETL Forge
project_spec.description:
SpotLight Streams ETL Forge is a high-throughput data engineering backbone designed for large-scale entertainment platforms that deliver personalized video, music, and interactive-game highlights. The system ingests raw audience interaction events (views, likes, in-game achievements, chat messages), media metadata, and third-party trend signals from multiple source feeds. Using a constellation of C-based microservices, the platform performs near-real-time and batch processing to cleanse, enrich, and transform this data into analytics-ready formats that drive recommendation engines, live overlay graphics, and dynamic content line-ups.

The microservices are arranged in a Pipeline Pattern layered over an Event-Streaming core: ingestion services push events to Kafka topics; parallel transformation workers apply Strategy Pattern–driven business rules for each entertainment modality (film, music, esports); validation and quality-check services observe data flows via the Observer Pattern, flagging anomalies to a monitoring dashboard. Output datasets land in a unified Data Lake (object storage + columnar files) and a curated Postgres warehouse optimized for BI queries. A CRON-driven scheduler orchestrates heavy nightly ETL jobs, while the same codebase supports millisecond-level stream processing for real-time leaderboards, making the solution versatile across on-demand and live entertainment use cases.
dependencies: librdkafka (Kafka C/C++ client) – event streaming transport
libpq (PostgreSQL C client) – relational storage access
libpqxx for optional C++ façade over libpq
Apache Arrow C GLib – in-memory columnar data interchange
jansson – fast JSON parsing/encoding for external APIs
cURL/libcurl – RESTful ingestion of third-party feeds
cronicle or custom CRON wrappers – job scheduling
Prometheus C client – runtime monitoring & alerting
uthash – lightweight hash tables for in-memory caches
